subject: maths
prompt_en: At 3 o'clock, do the two hands of a clock make a right angle?
prompt_hi: 3 baje ghadi ki dono suiyan kya right angle banati hain?
answer: Yes

subject: maths
prompt_en: I draw two square corners. One has arms 2 cm long and the other has arms 10 cm long. Guess: which angle is bigger?
prompt_hi: Main do square corner banata hoon. Ek ki lines 2 cm lambi hain aur doosre ki 10 cm. Guess karo: kaunsa angle bada hai?
answer: Neither: both are right angles, so they are the same

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why does drawing the arms of an angle longer not make the angle bigger?
prompt_hi: Angle ki lines ko lamba kar dene se angle bada kyun nahi hota?
answer: An angle is how wide the arms open (the amount of turn), not how long the arms are

subject: maths
prompt_en: Angle A opens just a little, like scissors opened slightly, but its arms are very long. Angle B is a square corner with short arms. Which angle is bigger?
prompt_hi: Angle A thoda sa khula hai, jaise kainchi thodi si khuli ho, par uski lines bahut lambi hain. Angle B ek square corner hai, chhoti lines ke saath. Kaunsa angle bada hai?
answer: Angle B

subject: maths
prompt_en: Which time has the clock hands making a right angle: 6 o'clock or 9 o'clock?
prompt_hi: Kis time pe ghadi ki suiyan right angle banati hain: 6 baje ya 9 baje?
answer: 9 o'clock

subject: maths
prompt_en: I turned a book so it is tilted like a diamond. I say its corners are not right angles any more. Am I right?
prompt_hi: Maine book ko tircha ghuma diya, ab woh diamond jaisi lagti hai. Main kehta hoon ab uske corners right angle nahi rahe. Kya main sahi hoon?
answer: No. Turning the book does not change its corners; they are still right angles

subject: maths
prompt_en: To draw a circle with a string and pencil, you hold one end of the string still with your finger. What is that still point called?
prompt_hi: String aur pencil se circle banane ke liye tum string ka ek sira ungli se dabake rakhte ho. Us point ko kya kehte hain?
answer: The centre

subject: maths
prompt_en: You tie a pencil to a 5 cm string and turn it around a pin, keeping the string tight. How far from the pin is every point on the circle?
prompt_hi: Tumne pencil ko 5 cm ki string se baandha aur string tight rakhkar pin ke chaaron taraf ghumaya. Circle ka har point pin se kitni door hai?
answer: 5 cm

subject: maths
prompt_en: An egg shape and the shape of a bangle. Which one is a circle, and how can you check?
prompt_hi: Ek ande ka shape aur ek chudi ka shape. Inmein circle kaunsa hai, aur kaise check karoge?
answer: The bangle; every point on it is the same distance from the centre

subject: maths
prompt_en: To draw a big circle in the playground, Ravi ties a 2 m rope to a peg and walks around with chalk tied at the other end. Why must he keep the rope tight?
prompt_hi: Playground mein bada circle banane ke liye Ravi 2 m ki rassi ek khoonte se baandhta hai aur doosre sire pe chalk lagakar chaaron taraf chalta hai. Rassi tight kyun rakhni padegi?
answer: So that every point he draws is exactly 2 m from the peg; a loose rope gives a wobbly shape that is not a circle

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach Golu how to check whether a corner is a right angle using a folded paper. Also tell him whether longer arms make an angle bigger.
prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao folded paper se kaise check karte hain ki corner right angle hai ya nahi. Aur use yeh bhi batao ki lambi lines se angle bada hota hai ya nahi.
answer: Fold paper twice to get a square corner, put it on the corner: if it fits exactly it is a right angle, if the corner is narrower it is less, if wider it is more; longer arms do not change the angle

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick! Name two things in your room that have right-angle corners.
prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Apne kamre mein do cheezein batao jinke corners right angle hain.
answer: Any two square-corner things, such as a book, a door, a window, a table top or a notebook

subject: maths
prompt_en: On a dot grid, you draw a line from one dot to the 5th dot in the same row. How many units long is the line?
prompt_hi: Dot grid pe tum ek dot se usi row ke 5th dot tak line banate ho. Line kitni units lambi hai?
answer: 4 units

subject: maths
prompt_en: I make an L shape on the grid using 4 squares. Now I turn the paper around. Guess: how many squares will the L have now?
prompt_hi: Main grid pe 4 squares se ek L shape banata hoon. Ab paper ghuma deta hoon. Guess karo: ab L mein kitne squares honge?
answer: Still 4

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why is a square turned to look like a diamond still a square?
prompt_hi: Ghumaya hua square, jo diamond jaisa dikhta hai, ab bhi square kyun hai?
answer: Its 4 sides are still equal and its corners are still right angles; turning does not change sides or angles

subject: maths
prompt_en: Shape A is a strip of 3 squares lying flat. Shape B is a strip of 3 squares standing up. Are they the same shape and size, or different?
prompt_hi: Shape A 3 squares ki ek patti hai jo leti hui hai. Shape B 3 squares ki patti hai jo khadi hai. Kya dono same shape aur size ke hain, ya alag?
answer: The same shape and size; B is A turned

subject: maths
prompt_en: Copy a T shape: 3 squares across the top and 2 squares going down from the middle square. How many squares are there in all?
prompt_hi: Ek T shape copy karo: upar 3 squares aur beech wale square se neeche 2 squares. Total kitne squares hain?

subject: maths
prompt_en: Riya wanted a line 3 units long on a dot grid, so she joined 3 dots. Is her line 3 units long?
prompt_hi: Riya ko dot grid pe 3 unit lambi line chahiye thi, isliye usne 3 dots joda. Kya uski line 3 unit lambi hai?
answer: No. Joining 3 dots makes a line 2 units long; she needs 4 dots

subject: maths
prompt_en: A tile pattern on a grid goes red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, and so on. Say it with letters R and B. What colour is the 7th tile?
prompt_hi: Grid pe tiles ka pattern hai: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, aur aise hi aage. Ise R aur B letters se bolo. 7th tile kis colour ki hogi?
answer: Red

subject: maths
prompt_en: A courtyard floor is 5 tiles long and 4 tiles wide. All the tiles along the border are red and the ones inside are white. How many white tiles are there?
prompt_hi: Ek aangan ka farsh 5 tiles lamba aur 4 tiles chauda hai. Kinare ki saari tiles red hain aur andar wali white. Kitni white tiles hain?

subject: maths
prompt_en: On a square grid, line A goes along one side of a small square. Line B goes slanting from one corner to the opposite corner of the same square. Are they the same length?
prompt_hi: Square grid pe line A ek chhote square ki ek side ke saath jaati hai. Line B usi square ke ek corner se saamne wale corner tak tirchi jaati hai. Kya dono ki lambai barabar hai?
answer: No, the slanting line B is longer

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach Golu how to copy a shape exactly on a dot grid.
prompt_hi: Golu ko sikhao dot grid pe shape bilkul same kaise copy karte hain.
answer: Start at a dot, count the gaps (units) along each side of the shape and draw the same number of gaps in the same direction; check the corners match

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick! If I turn a rectangle on the grid, does the number of squares inside it change?
prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Agar main grid pe rectangle ghuma doon, toh andar ke squares ki ginti badlegi?
answer: No, it stays the same

subject: maths
prompt_en: You look straight down at a steel glass standing on the table. What shape do you see?
prompt_hi: Tum table pe khade steel ke glass ko seedha upar se dekhte ho. Kaunsa shape dikhta hai?
answer: A circle (the rim of the glass)

subject: maths
prompt_en: A drum shaped like a cylinder stands on the floor. Guess its front view: a circle, a rectangle, or a triangle?
prompt_hi: Cylinder jaisa ek dhol zameen pe khada hai. Guess karo, saamne se kaisa dikhega: circle, rectangle, ya triangle?
answer: A rectangle

subject: maths
prompt_en: A birthday cap (cone) and a dabba (cylinder) both stand on a table. What does each look like from the top?
prompt_hi: Ek birthday cap (cone) aur ek dabba (cylinder) dono table pe khade hain. Upar se dono kaise dikhte hain?
answer: Both look like circles (the cap has a dot in the middle at its tip)

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why does a glass look like a circle from the top but like a rectangle from the front?
prompt_hi: Glass upar se circle jaisa aur saamne se rectangle jaisa kyun dikhta hai?
answer: From the top you see only its round mouth; from the front you see its height and width

subject: maths
prompt_en: A dice sits on the table. What do its top, front and side views look like?
prompt_hi: Ek dice table pe rakha hai. Uske top, front aur side view kaise dikhte hain?
answer: All three are squares

subject: maths
prompt_en: I said the top view of a gas cylinder standing up is a rectangle. Am I right?
prompt_hi: Maine kaha khade gas cylinder ka top view rectangle hai. Kya main sahi hoon?
answer: No. From the top it looks like a circle; the rectangle is its front view

subject: maths
prompt_en: An object looks like a triangle from the front and a circle from the top. Which is it: a cone, a cylinder, or a cube?
prompt_hi: Ek cheez saamne se triangle aur upar se circle jaisi dikhti hai. Woh kya hai: cone, cylinder, ya cube?
answer: A cone

subject: maths
prompt_en: From the top, an object looks like a square. From the front, it looks like a triangle. What could it be?
prompt_hi: Upar se ek cheez square jaisi dikhti hai. Saamne se triangle jaisi. Woh kya ho sakti hai?
answer: A pyramid with a square base, like a tent

subject: maths
prompt_en: A brick lies flat on the ground. What shape is its front view?
prompt_hi: Ek eent zameen pe leti hui hai. Saamne se woh kis shape ki dikhti hai?
answer: A rectangle

subject: maths
prompt_en: Asked for the top view of a matchbox lying on a table, Mini drew a box with its top and two sides showing. Is that the top view?
prompt_hi: Mini se table pe padi maachis ki dibbi ka top view banane ko kaha, toh usne ek dabba banaya jisme upar aur do sides dikh rahi hain. Kya yeh top view hai?
answer: No. The top view is just a flat rectangle

subject: maths
prompt_en: Teach Chintu how to find the top view of an object, using a glass as your example.
prompt_hi: Chintu ko sikhao kisi cheez ka top view kaise nikalte hain. Glass ka example lo.
answer: Look straight down from above; draw only the flat outline facing up, with no sides; a glass gives a circle

subject: maths
prompt_en: Quick! What is the top view of a cylinder-shaped dabba standing up?
prompt_hi: Jaldi batao! Khade hue cylinder jaise dabbe ka top view kya hai?
answer: A circle

subject: maths
prompt_en: Columns are A, B, C, D, E from left to right, and rows are 1 to 5 going up. Meena stands at A1. She goes 3 steps right and 2 steps up. Where is she now?
prompt_hi: Columns left se right A, B, C, D, E hain, aur rows neeche se upar 1 se 5. Meena A1 pe khadi hai. Woh 3 step right aur 2 step upar jaati hai. Ab woh kahan hai?
answer: D3

subject: maths
prompt_en: Raju walks towards you, facing you. He raises his right hand. Guess: is that hand on your left side or your right side?
prompt_hi: Raju tumhari taraf chalta aa raha hai, tumhe face kar raha hai. Woh apna right haath uthata hai. Guess karo: woh haath tumhare left side hai ya right side?
answer: On my left side

subject: maths
prompt_en: Why did Raju's right hand appear on your left side?
prompt_hi: Raju ka right haath tumhare left side pe kyun dikha?
answer: Because he faces the opposite way to me; when we face each other, his right is on my left

subject: maths
prompt_en: From A1: path P is '2 steps right, then 3 steps up'. Path Q is '3 steps right, then 2 steps up'. Do they reach the same square?
prompt_hi: A1 se: rasta P hai '2 step right, phir 3 step upar'. Rasta Q hai '3 step right, phir 2 step upar'. Kya dono ek hi square pe pahunchte hain?
answer: No. P reaches C4 and Q reaches D3

subject: maths
prompt_en: Start at B2. Go 2 steps right and 3 steps up. Where are you?
prompt_hi: B2 se shuru karo. 2 step right aur 3 step upar jao. Tum kahan ho?
answer: D5
